clue.text: Old-style rule, prior to anything being written down?

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before or prior to
a script is any text that has been written down

explanation.surface: A puzzled historian wonders whether an ancient regulation existed before people could write.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the loose sense of SCRIPT: any written text, not just a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A prescript is an archaic word for an ordinance or rule laid down in advance.

clue.text: Band's helper gets fee finally after radio broadcast

indicators.note: after places the piece from fee behind the rearranged letters
broadcast means scattered about, so the letters of radio are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word fee

explanation.surface: A band's crew member gets paid once a radio show goes out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like the radio's own activity, but it signals the anagram of RADIO, giving ROADI.
explanation.definitionFit: A touring band's road crew member, who sets up and carries the gear, is called by this name.

clue.text: Son is given meat, not a thick slice

parts.note: liver is offal eaten as meat

explanation.surface: A boy is served meat, but only a thin portion of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin narrow piece cut off something is a sliver, the opposite of a thick slice.

clue.text: Give an account of soldiers deceased

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
the late so-and-so means someone who has died

explanation.surface: A report is given about soldiers who have died.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate or recount a story is to give an account of events.

clue.text: Artist left with a tinier part needing to be changed

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: the words a tinier part must be altered, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter leaves, taking a smaller role that has to be reworked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a departure but is the nautical side; 'needing to be changed' signals the anagram, giving RAITPAINTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who paints likenesses of people is one particular kind of artist.

clue.text: Brit collaring little pests, an officer

indicators.note: collaring means grabbing round the neck, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: Pom is Australian slang for a British person
lice are tiny parasitic insects
taken as written

explanation.surface: A British man grabs some small vermin, as an official might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brit' uses Australian slang for an English person, which solvers outside Britain may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: A constable or other member of the police force is an officer of the law.

clue.text: Heavenly body is remote, I do fancy

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, taken as written
anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone admits to admiring a distant star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' reads as 'I do like it', but it signals the anagram of REMOTE I DO.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rocky or metallic object travelling through space is a heavenly body.

clue.text: Being efficient, manage to protect maiden needing shelter

indicators.note: to protect means to surround, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to cope is to manage
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
a tent is a canvas shelter

explanation.surface: Being efficient means coping, guarding a young woman who needs a roof over her head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' is a link word before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone capable of doing a task well is both efficient and able.

clue.text: Part of SA gets sun and zero water — zero!

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for sun or Sunday
the figure zero looks like the letter O
to water something is to wet it
zero again looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A region of South Africa gets sunshine and no rainfall whatsoever.
explanation.definitionFit: This township near Johannesburg is a district of South Africa.

clue.text: In Cyprus a post's secured a small vessel

indicators.note: in tells us the next pieces sit within the country code

parts.note: CY is the international code for Cyprus
a pillar is an upright post

explanation.surface: In Cyprus, a mooring post has been fixed for a little boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a boat, but here it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The finest blood vessels in the body are the tiny tubes linking arteries and veins.

clue.text: Accident when little Philip's swallowed Romanian money

indicators.note: swallowed means taken inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: Pip is a pet form of the name Philip
the leu is the currency of Romania

explanation.surface: A mishap occurs when a small boy gulps down a foreign coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A multiple-vehicle crash on a road is a collision or accident.

clue.text: List minister of religion as being into home improvements?

indicators.note: being into means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is home improvement work
a rector is a parish priest

explanation.surface: A vicar is listed as an enthusiast of household repairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being into' reads as being keen on something, but it is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of names and addresses, such as a phone book, is a list.

clue.text: Bishop getting in the way of walkers, beast!

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: walkers travel on their feet
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A clergyman obstructs hikers on a path, and someone calls him a brute.
explanation.definitionFit: A small carnivorous mammal used for hunting rabbits is an animal or beast.

clue.text: Days before Christmas with university about to provide exciting experience

parts.note: Advent is the church season leading up to Christmas
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: The run-up to Christmas at college promises to be thrilling.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade or daring undertaking is an exciting experience.

clue.text: Like 20, I am the bee's knees with musical coming up

parts.note: I'm is short for I am
it means the very best thing, as in 'that's it'

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means read from bottom to top, so the musical's name is reversed

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical

explanation.surface: A self-satisfied performer claims to be the best now that a show is opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' reverses EVITA to ATIVE. The definition points to 20-across, a mimic.
explanation.definitionFit: Clue 20 is a copier; copying behaviour is mimicking, so like it means mimicking.

clue.text: I'm one involved with cost

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder; the apostrophe adds no letter
anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A professional speaks about their job, which is all about prices.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: 'involved' rearranges I'M ONE COST.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist in money, markets and resources studies costs for a living.

clue.text: A little female dog companion let loose

indicators.note: let loose means set free, so these letters are released from the word

parts.note: a bitch is a female dog
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A small female dog's pal is released.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit is a small amount, so 'a little' and 'a bit' are interchangeable.

clue.text: Beastly sound from a sailor capsizing

indicators.note: capsizing means turning over, so in a down clue these letters go upside down

parts.note: taken as written
AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: An animal noise comes from a seaman whose boat is overturning.
explanation.definitionFit: The bleat of a sheep is the sound a farm animal makes.

clue.text: Part of formal attire for the match

definitions.meaning: a bow or neck band worn with a suit
a cup game, as in a fourth-round football fixture

explanation.surface: Someone dresses up smartly for the big game.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a neckwear item and a knockout sports fixture share this one short word.

clue.text: To administer a Co. differently, move towards giving everyone a say

definitions.text: move towards giving everyone a say

indicators.note: differently means arranged another way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written; the full stop adds no letter

explanation.surface: Running a company in a new style is meant to give all staff a voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Making something democratic means extending the vote and control to all its members.

clue.text: Clumsy person in a gym

parts.note: taken as written
PE, physical education, is school gym class

explanation.surface: An awkward individual is seen working out at the fitness centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a great oaf or lummox, a big clumsy lout, is the informal use here.

clue.text: Process of 'refuelling' — what you need to get 'ot

indicators.note: 'ot is hot with its first letter dropped, a cockney accent, signalling the same letter goes

parts.note: a central heating system is what you need to get warm

explanation.surface: A cheeky note says how to fill up and also how to warm a house.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H in ''ot' tells you to drop the H from the warming word too, as a cockney would.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking food is refuelling the body, a jokey way to describe a meal.

clue.text: Blasted theologian restricting English composer

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: DD is a Doctor of Divinity
Thomas Arne wrote Rule, Britannia!

explanation.surface: A damned scholar of religion is confining an English musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Darned and blasted are both mild exclamatory curses meaning damned.

clue.text: Starter perhaps for run

definitions.meaning: a starter is an example of one stage of a meal
the route or progress something follows, as in the river's run

explanation.surface: A first dish is served for a sprint.
explanation.definitionFit: A meal has several dishes in stages, and a route or progression is also this word.

clue.text: The female's at home, upset with a medical condition

parts.note: her means belonging to a female

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so in a down clue these letters go upwards

parts.note: in means at home
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman is home and unhappy, suffering from an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A rupture where an organ pokes through the abdominal wall is a medical complaint.

clue.text: A person, if misshapen, should get particular garments

indicators.note: misshapen means badly formed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, taken as written
anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: An oddly shaped individual needs specially made clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleeveless aprons or dresses worn over clothing are a particular kind of garment.

clue.text: Around the walls of tabernacle see most unusual symbols

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece is placed outside the other
unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, taken as written

indicators.note: walls are the outer edges, so the first and last letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: Inside a sacred tent, visitors see the rarest emblems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' turns the fodder into TOMS; 'walls of' takes only the outside letters; 'Around' wraps the first round the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Carved poles or objects standing for a clan or spirit are emblems or symbols.

clue.text: Unsettled person that is to shout angrily about money

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is
tin is old British slang for cash
to rant is to shout angrily

explanation.surface: A restless person rages about cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller who moves from place to place and has no fixed home is unsettled.

clue.text: Forcibly carry off very little one covered in spots?

indicators.note: covered in means enclosed, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots
V is the short form of very, little marking the abbreviation
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tiny child with chickenpox is snatched away.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic sense of this verb is to seize and abduct someone by force.

clue.text: Track badly fouled up with wire

indicators.note: fouled up means messed up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, taken as written
anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A path is tangled up by loose fencing wire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'fouled up' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A path for horse riders and walkers across the countryside is a track.
